analysis: The method `getProperty(String propertyName)` first checks `immutableDefaultProperties`, then queries a database using `propertyName`, then checks `defaultProperties`, and finally calls `System.getProperty(propertyName)`. The `propertyName` parameter is used directly in `System.getProperty` without any null check or empty validation. The method catches `SQLException` but does not handle or avoid the exceptions declared in the `System.getProperty` API. There is no try-catch around the `System.getProperty` call, so any exceptions from it propagate. The calling context provides no prior validation or checks that would avoid these exceptions.
remark: The exceptions are not avoided because the code does not validate that `propertyName` is non-null or non-empty before calling `System.getProperty`. A null `propertyName` will cause a `NullPointerException`. An empty `propertyName` will cause an `IllegalArgumentException`. A `SecurityException` can occur if a security manager is present and access to the property is denied; there is no check or handler for this condition.
